meetings.title: Session 1 (part 1): BIOGLOW theme immersion + mission model build begins
goals: Explore the BIOGLOW biodiversity theme and how FLL Challenge works
Begin building all robot game mission models from official instructions
activities: Watch BIOGLOW season videos (FIRST LEGO League YouTube playlist)
Read Engineering Notebook pp. 3-9 on how FLL Challenge works; vocabulary: mission model, project spark, innovation project

Build mission models from bags 1-10 (M01 Drone Survey, M02 Exploding Seeds, M03 Flip the Rock, M04 Lucky Leaves, M05 Reaching Roots, M06 Leafcutter Frenzy, M07 Humongous Fungus) split in pairs; coach inspects/tests each model
Explore how models connect to Project Sparks (EN p6); write model notes on EN p10
Reflection questions + clean up (bag unfinished builds)
deliverables: Roughly half the mission models built and tested

meetings.title: Session 1 (part 2): finish mission models + field setup
goals: Complete all 15 mission models and the three interchangeable dock models
Set up the game field exactly per Robot Game Rulebook pp. 7-8
activities: Build remaining models from bags 11-24 (M08 Tangled, M09 Research Platform, M10 Fragile Microhabitats both placements, M11 Window to the Past, M12 Forest Elder, M13 Keystone Species, M14 Seeds of Renewal, M15 Biocentric Architecture, three docks)
Lay mat aligned to bottom wall, place Dual Lock on wireframe marks, seat models on outlines; watch Field Setup Video
Wireframe audit using the A-J x 1-6 grid diagram; sort six Precision Tokens into a referee bag
Share at the mat: how models connect to the BIOGLOW theme; reflection + clean up
deliverables: All 15 mission models + docks built, field wireframe-verified (Checkpoint 1 model requirement met)

meetings.title: Session 2: team goals + Training Camp 1 (Driving Around)
goals: Build a driving base that drives forward/backward and turns
Record team goals and surface first innovation project ideas
activities: Core Value: Discovery; record team goals + what members hope to learn on Team Progress sheet (EN p8, Start Here)
Vocabulary: robot, code, controller; coach flags that programs downloaded to the controller cannot be pulled back — keep sources in the app
SPIKE app optional Tutorial Activities 1-6 (only if needed), then Competition Ready Training Camp 1: Driving Around
Drive the robot to a mission model and back home; take skill notes
Discuss project ideas sparked by the mission models; collect signed consent forms sent home at kickoff
Reflect, share at the mat, clean up

meetings.title: Session 3: problem statement locked (TMG deadline) + Training Camp 2
goals: Decide and record the innovation project problem statement (hard TMG deadline this session)
Code the robot to handle objects and attempt a first mission
activities: Review project info (EN p5) and Project Sparks (EN p6); every member shares ideas; pick a problem everyone supports
WRITE the problem statement on the Innovation Project Planning sheet (EN p29)
SPIKE app Competition Ready Training Camp 2: Playing with Objects (sensor obstacle-avoid + powered attachment)
Attempt a first mission with an attachment; discuss how the new skills transfer to the robot game
Reflect (what research is needed, which missions next), share at the mat, clean up
deliverables: Problem statement recorded on EN p29

meetings.title: Session 4: research plan + Training Camp 3 (Reacting to Lines) — Checkpoint 1
goals: Plan what research is needed on existing solutions
Detect and use mat lines; begin drafting mission strategy
activities: Vocabulary: mission strategy, autonomous, match (2.5-minute timed period earning points)
Identify research sources: websites, videos, books, magazines, personal stories, interviews; decide how findings feed the solution
SPIKE app Competition Ready Training Camp 3: Reacting to Lines; map the mat's black path segments as navigation aids
Attempt a different mission; begin the mission-strategy draft (which missions, what order); launch from a consistent spot in a launch area
Coach runs Checkpoint 1 review after the meeting: team bonded, all models built/secured, missions and rules reviewed, problem statement written, goals reviewed

meetings.title: Session 5 (part 1, project track): research with sources + choose the solution
goals: Research the chosen problem with cited sources
Decide new-vs-improved and select ONE solution to develop
activities: Core Value: Teamwork — short team-building activity
Vocabulary: solution, attachment, engineering design process
Research the problem on EN pp. 14 and 29, citing title/author/website for each source
Decide whether to propose a new solution or improve an existing one; select exactly one solution; reference the rubrics
Rotating table time: continue attempting missions from Sessions 3-4
Reflect (who can we talk to about the problem?), share, clean up
deliverables: Research captured on EN p14/p29 with sources

meetings.title: Session 5 (part 2, robot track): Guided Mission until consistent
goals: Complete the SPIKE app Guided Mission reliably
Grow the mission repertoire and organize attachments
activities: SPIKE app Competition Ready Guided Mission (SPIKE Prime); practice until it runs consistently — its program transfers to other missions
Optional: Assembling an Advanced Driving Base lesson
Attempt other missions; change one thing at a time; test program changes in small steps
Bag and label attachments by mission number; name and organize programs clearly
Reflect (what the guided mission teaches about Coopetition/transfer), share at the mat, clean up
deliverables: Attachments bagged and labeled per mission

meetings.title: Session 6 (part 1): Halfway There milestone + solution development plan
goals: Complete the mid-season 'Halfway There' checkpoint
Plan how the solution will be developed and prototyped
activities: Core Value: Innovation; vocabulary: prototype, pseudocode
Complete 'Halfway There' section of the Team Progress sheet (EN p8)
Plan solution development on the Innovation Project Planning sheet (EN p29, Solution Planning box); keep tracking sources
List the materials needed for the prototype; coach arranges craft materials for Session 7
Rotating table time: continue practicing missions
Reflect, share, clean up
deliverables: EN p29 Solution Planning box completed

meetings.title: Session 6 (part 2): mission strategy on the mat + pseudocode
goals: Build the mission-strategy plan around easiest-scoring missions first
Write and test pseudocode for a chosen mission
activities: Re-watch the Robot Game Missions video and review the Robot Game Rulebook together (missions pp. 8-12, rules pp. 13-18)

Map strategy on the mat with sticky notes/planning cards: point value vs difficulty vs table position vs reliability; include the M13-15 dock-placement decision and bonus targets (M15 Environmental Bonus, M04 katydid bonus)
Complete the Pseudocode sheet (EN p28) for a selected mission; upload and test the program in the SPIKE app
Combine multiple missions per run where possible; track run times
Reflect (how documentation helps at judging), share, clean up
deliverables: Mission-strategy plan drafted with run clusters

meetings.title: Session 7 (part 1): build the innovation project prototype
goals: Create the prototype model or detailed drawing of the solution
Document the development process for judging
activities: Core Value: Gracious Professionalism — coach points out lived examples
Vocabulary: rubric, feedback, improve
Draw the solution and explain how it solves the problem; build the prototype model or detailed drawing (need not be functional, but the team must explain how it would work in detail)
Document all changes and process on EN p29 — judges want to hear the journey
Rotating table time: continue mission practice
Reflect (can we describe the solution simply? who gives us feedback?), share, clean up
deliverables: Prototype model or detailed drawing created

meetings.title: Session 7 (part 2): robot iteration + launch-position discipline
goals: Iterate robot and attachments across attempted missions
Choose the launch-area starting position and mission ownership
activities: Inventory attempted vs remaining missions (EN p30 mission notes, photocopied per mission)
Test and improve robot + attachments; one program per new mission or combine missions into one program
Assign mission ownership to members; if sharing one robot, members code on individual devices and take turns
Pick launch-area starting position (red/left vs blue/right) per run — whole robot must fit inside the launch area; keep placement notes
Change one thing at a time; narrate the program as the robot moves to debug
Reflect, share robot skills at the mat, clean up

meetings.title: Session 8 (part 1): external feedback on the solution
goals: Share the solution outside the team and collect feedback
Decide which feedback to act on and iterate
activities: Core Value: Inclusion — how does the team make sure every voice is heard?
Vocabulary: evaluate, expert, test
Share the solution with others (survey, people affected by the problem, expert interview/webinar — expert scheduled 1-2 weeks ahead); record feedback on EN p29 (Feedback box)
Decide which feedback to apply; test the updated solution if possible; identify who the solution is for
Rotating table time: mission practice
Reflect (what changes after feedback?), share, clean up
deliverables: External feedback recorded on EN p29

meetings.title: Session 8 (part 2): reliable mission programs — Checkpoint 2
goals: Add another mission to the strategy and make it reliable
Pass Checkpoint 2 and put rubrics in the team's hands
activities: Pick another mission, fit it into the mission strategy, iterate program + attachments until reliable; document design/testing per mission
Prefer simple repeatable designs; combine missions per run; keep robot-placement notes
Decide the draft mission run order for matches

Coach Checkpoint 2 after the meeting: all Session 1-8 robot lessons done; project problem researched, solution designed and shared for feedback; PRINT judging rubrics, scoresheets, and the judging session flowchart from Season Resources and hand the judging documents to the team
Reflect (how have Core Values shaped robot + project?), share, clean up
deliverables: Rubrics/scoresheets/judging flowchart printed and handed to the team

meetings.title: Session 9: iterate both tracks + back up programs
goals: Refine mission strategy on the mat and iterate robot and project from testing/feedback
Understand which rubric criteria feed the Core Values score
activities: Core Value: Impact; EN p22 prompt on positive influence; vocabulary: judge, field
Try to fit one more mission into the 2:30 window; verify the strategy covers all target missions
Iterate robot code/attachments and the innovation project solution; document every change
Back up all programs to USB stick or online storage
Review rubrics to learn which criteria count toward the Core Values score; discuss how to explain what is innovative to judges
Reflect, share, clean up

meetings.title: Rules mastery + launch-routine and inspection drill (coach rules priority)
goals: Master the Robot Game Rulebook rules as they will be refereed
Drill launch routine and the one-launch-area inspection bonus
activities: Rules-lawyer quiz on high-cost rules: M04 katydid zero condition, no breaking models/separating Dual Lock, single-motion freeable combinations, objects captured after last launch go to the referee, points scored by hand outside home don't count, free final stop-in-place exception
Glossary quiz: launch, interruption, technician, autonomous, home

Launch-routine drill: two technicians per home area, no side switching, launches fully inside the launch area, clean interruptions/relaunches, when a stop costs a precision token (6 tokens: 1=10/2=15/3=25/4=35/5=50/6=50)

One-launch-area packing design: all equipment in ONE launch area under 12 in for the 20-point inspection bonus; mock equipment inspection including identifying the team-built M13 keystone species model (bag 20)
Table time with remaining minutes; reflect + clean up
deliverables: Packing layout for the 20-point inspection bonus

meetings.title: Session 10 (part 1): build the innovation project presentation
goals: Plan the 5-minute innovation project presentation against the official rubric
Create scripts and visual displays
activities: Core Value: Coopetition; EN p23 prompt; vocabulary: presentation, script
Read the innovation project rubric to learn what the 5-minute live presentation must include (problem, research, solution, iteration from feedback, impact)
Write the presentation outline/script — every member participates; script copies for each member
Create visual displays (slideshow, poster, play/skit allowed; props/costumes optional); solution drawing/model ready to show judges
Consult the judging session flowchart for timing
Reflect, share, clean up

meetings.title: Session 10 (part 2): first full timed 2:30 matches
goals: Run complete timed robot game matches and score them
Harden the strategy against event-day variability
activities: Practice full 2.5-minute robot games with all working missions on a timer; count missions completed
Score each run with the official scoresheet / Official Scoring Calculator
Check attachments are organized and easy to grab mid-match; everyone participates
Dock-variability runs: execute M13/M14/M15 programs with interchangeable models moved between Mine, City, and Farm docks; randomize M04 katydid/leaves and vary M02 tube orientation before runs
Field reset to wireframe-exact state between runs (timed)
Reflect, share, clean up

meetings.title: Session 11 (part 1): robot design explanation + Event Time milestone
goals: Plan the 5-minute robot design explanation against the robot design rubric
Complete the 'Event Time' section of the Team Progress sheet
activities: Core Value: Fun; vocabulary: explanation, robot design
Complete 'Event Time' section of Team Progress sheet (EN p8)
Read the robot design rubric; outline/script the 5-minute explanation covering mission strategy, robot design/build, programs, iteration/testing evidence, and EVERY member's contribution
Practice explaining robot design and strategy WITHOUT the game field (as at judging)
Rotating table time: mission practice
Reflect, share, clean up

meetings.title: Session 11 (part 2): presentation practice + match roles locked
goals: Practice the project presentation with feedback
Assign who runs the robot during matches
activities: Run the innovation project presentation; collect and apply feedback; ensure everyone has a part
Decide robot operator/technician assignments per match (two per home area, fixed sides)
Contact the event organizer now if any accommodations are needed (TMG: no later than Session 11)
Continue timed 2:30 match practice with scoresheets
Reflect (which robot parts show the Engineering Design Process?), share, clean up

meetings.title: Session 12 (part 1): full judging dress rehearsal
goals: Rehearse the complete judging session end-to-end with outside feedback
activities: Review team goals on EN p8 — did we achieve them?; review 'Prepare for Your Event' (EN p26) and 'Rubrics & Scoresheets' (EN p27)
Rehearse the full judging presentation: 5-minute innovation project presentation + 5-minute robot design explanation, timed per the judging session flowchart, with judges' Q&A simulated
Get feedback from coach/mentor/parents (or another team) and iterate scripts
Verify every member can explain the work per the rubrics
Reflect, share, clean up
deliverables: Both 5-minute presentations rehearsed end-to-end with feedback

meetings.title: Session 12 (part 2): scored matches + contingency plan + packing list
goals: Run multiple scored practice matches with correct program run order
Build the mission-failure contingency plan and event packing checklist
activities: Run multiple 2:30 matches; calculate points with the p27 scoresheets; drill running programs in the right order
Build the contingency plan: alternate missions to run if a mission fails mid-match

Write the event packing checklist: robot + attachments (labeled bags), device with programs + chargers, project materials/prototype/visuals, scripts, robot programming notes, one sheet of program-notes paper per home area, spare batteries/charged power pack, microSD
Final paperwork sweep ahead of the Oct 31 deadline (registrations, notebook worksheets)
Reflect, share, clean up

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 1: full match simulation with referee
goals: Simulate event-format robot game matches under real refereeing
Establish a scored best-of-three baseline
activities: Full 2.5-minute matches on a timer with a parent acting as referee; six precision tokens tracked per Rulebook (one lost per out-of-home interruption; free final stop-in-place)
Simulate best-of-three format — only the best score counts; enter every score in the Official Scoring Calculator
Model Gracious Professionalism behaviors as referees will score them (2/3/4 at every match)
Timed field-reset drill between matches using the printed 4-up Field Setup Guide as checklist
Post-match score review with the 'referee' documenting results WITH the team (agreement makes it official)
Debrief: log every failed/marginal mission
deliverables: Failed-mission list for the week's fixes

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 2: pit/table logistics + mock inspection — paperwork closes Oct 31
goals: Drill the event-day equipment inspection and setup window
Confirm all paperwork is complete before the Oct 31 deadline
activities: Mock equipment inspection: everything fits within the two launch areas under 12 in (305 mm); attempt the ONE-launch-area 20-point bonus layout; identify the team-built M13 keystone species model to the 'inspector'

Drill the couple-of-minutes setup window: distribute loose models/equipment between the two home areas, place robot, calibrate sensors on the mat, choose M13-15 dock placement, ask the referee to check the field
Fixed technician groups practice (left/right, no switching; max two per home area)
Referee-interaction etiquette: alerting to field problems BEFORE the match, score-review agreement
Coach verifies with the team: registrations, consent forms, notebook worksheets, backups — everything due 2026-10-31 is done
Short judging touch-up with remaining minutes
deliverables: Inspection + setup routine drilled to time

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 3: full judging simulation + matches
goals: Run the judging session exactly per the flowchart, in case the scrimmage offers judging
Keep match sharpness with randomized field conditions
activities: Full judging simulation: 5-minute innovation project presentation + 5-minute robot design explanation (without the field) + Q&A, timed per the judging session flowchart, with outside feedback against the rubrics
Verify every member has a speaking part and each member's contribution is described
Two scored 2:30 matches with randomization drill: 'referee' randomizes M04 katydid/leaves and varies M02 tube orientation; rotate M13-15 dock assignments
Precision-token and GP behaviors reinforced
Debrief both halves; update scripts and run order
deliverables: Judging session runs inside time limits with all members participating

meetings.title: Scrimmage rehearsal 4: final polish + pack for Sunday
goals: Close remaining gaps and pack for the Nov 8 scrimmage
Verify rules currency via Challenge Updates
activities: Read the latest Challenge Updates and re-verify strategy/scores against them (updates supersede the Rulebook)
Complete the 'Summarize Your Project' box (EN p29) — required before the event
Final short matches: first-choice run order, contingency-plan walkthrough, one more inspection + setup-window rehearsal

Pack against the checklist: robot, labeled attachment bags, device + chargers, backed-up programs, program-notes paper (one sheet per home area), spare batteries/power pack, microSD, prototype/visuals/scripts, scoresheets/calculator, printed Field Setup Guide
Confirm Sunday logistics with families: arrival time, travel, roles; charge and update the controller
deliverables: EN p29 fully complete incl. Summarize Your Project

meetings.title: SCRIMMAGE — dry run of the main event (robot game + judging if offered)
goals: Compete in event-format matches treating it as a real qualifier
Capture every scoresheet, GP score, and judge/referee comment for the debrief
activities: Arrive early; check the tournament field and alert the referee to problems BEFORE matches; note the event's M13-15 dock assignment and select matching program variants
Equipment inspection: go for the one-launch-area 20-point bonus; identify the keystone species model
Play all offered 2.5-minute matches best-of-three style; fixed technician groups; track precision tokens; run the contingency plan if a mission fails
Demonstrate Gracious Professionalism at every match and Coopetition with other teams (M07 cooperative bonus with the opposing table)
Deliver the judging session if offered (5-min project + 5-min robot design per flowchart)
Record all scores in the scoring calculator; review results with referees; collect all feedback in the notebook
deliverables: Official-style scoresheets, GP scores, and judging feedback captured

meetings.title: Scrimmage debrief: build the improvement backlog
goals: Convert scrimmage results into a prioritized robot/mission and judging improvement plan
activities: Review every scrimmage scoresheet vs practice baselines: which missions scored, which failed or were marginal, where precision tokens were lost
Review GP scores and any judging feedback against the rubrics
Rank fixes by points-per-effort; decide whether to add, drop, or reorder missions in the strategy (revisit the M13-15 dock decision and bonus targets)
Update the Innovation Project and robot design scripts with lessons learned; document everything in the notebook as judging evidence
Set the improvement backlog for the remaining weeks

meetings.title: Robot iteration 1: fix top scrimmage misses
goals: Repair the highest-value failed missions from the scrimmage
activities: Work the top of the backlog: iterate programs/attachments for missions that failed at the scrimmage; change one thing at a time and document each change
Re-time affected runs; verify combined runs still fit 2:30
Re-verify launch positions and the one-launch-area packing layout after any attachment changes
Back up updated programs to USB/online
Timed scored run at close to measure progress

meetings.title: Judging improvements from scrimmage feedback
goals: Revise both 5-minute presentations using scrimmage feedback and the rubrics
activities: Rework the innovation project presentation and robot design explanation where judges/observers flagged gaps; re-check each rubric criterion, especially those feeding the Core Values score
Add concrete Core Values examples from the scrimmage (Coopetition, Gracious Professionalism moments)
Re-rehearse both presentations timed per the flowchart; confirm every member's part
Refresh visual displays/prototype explanation as needed
Short table block to keep match rhythm
deliverables: Updated scripts and visuals for both judging deliverables

meetings.title: Robot iteration 2 + full timed matches
goals: Attempt to add one more mission if it fits 2:30
Re-establish scored full-match consistency
activities: Continue the backlog: next mission fixes or one additional mission if the time budget allows
Multiple full 2:30 scored matches with the scoring calculator; precision tokens tracked; randomized M04/M02 and rotated docks
Drill program run order and attachment handoffs; keep run-time log
Field reset drill between matches; document iteration in the notebook
deliverables: Consistent scored matches at or above scrimmage best

meetings.title: Combined rehearsal before Thanksgiving break
goals: Bank a complete judging + match rehearsal before the week off
activities: Full judging run-through (both 5-minute presentations + Q&A) with outside feedback
Two scored 2:30 matches, best-score tracking
Record all remaining gaps to attack in December; back up programs
Assign light optional home practice (scripts, parts review) over the break — with parent permission/supervision for any linked resources

meetings.title: Re-entry: Challenge Updates check + rust removal
goals: Re-verify rules currency and shake off the break
Confirm main-event logistics as the date firms up
activities: Read the latest Challenge Updates ('especially important leading up to your event') and re-verify strategy and expected scores against them
Full field audit against the wireframe diagram; check controller firmware/app updates; recharge everything
Full scored 2:30 matches to rebuild timing and consistency
Coach: pin down main-event date/type/organizer, start/end times, event-specific requirements, and travel (Final Checkpoint items begin)
Quick rules-refresher quiz
deliverables: Strategy re-verified against current Challenge Updates

meetings.title: Peak dress rehearsal 1: full event simulation
goals: Run judging and best-of-three matches as one continuous event simulation
activities: Judging session per the flowchart: 5-min innovation project + 5-min robot design (no field) + Q&A, with feedback from coach/mentor/parents
Best-of-three match simulation: inspection (one-launch-area bonus), setup window, three scored 2:30 matches with precision tokens and GP modeling
Contingency-plan execution drill: deliberately 'fail' a mission and switch to alternates
Debrief and log final adjustments only — no new features from here
deliverables: Complete event simulation executed; final-fix list only

meetings.title: Final Checkpoint + last dress rehearsal (flexes with main-event date TBD)
goals: Close the TMG Final Checkpoint
Lock everything for event day
activities: Final Checkpoint review: event times confirmed, travel arranged, families invited, event-specific requirements reviewed, every member able to explain the work per the rubrics
Final judging run-through and 1-2 scored matches; verify program run order and technician assignments
Finalize the materials checklist: robot + attachments, project materials/prototype/visuals, scripts, programming notes, chargers, spares, microSD, notes paper
Verify backups current; charge/update controller
If the main event lands earlier in December, swap this content earlier and use freed dates as post-event buffer
deliverables: Packed and locked for the main event

meetings.title: Taper: light run-throughs and confidence
goals: Keep sharpness without introducing risk before the main event
activities: Light run-throughs of the first-choice match runs only; no design changes
One relaxed pass of each presentation focusing on delivery and fun (Core Value)
Inspection + setup-window drill one final time; re-read the contingency plan
Confirm everyone's event-day roles (judging parts + match technicians); final Challenge Updates glance
Celebrate readiness — review how far the team has come vs the p8 goals
deliverables: Team event-ready: runs, roles, and materials confirmed

meetings.title: Wrap-up part 1: celebration + reflection
goals: Celebrate the season and process event feedback
activities: Team celebration (TMG post-season wrap-up)
Discuss rubric scores and judge/referee feedback from the main event; compare against the season goals on EN p8
Share the experience — what each member learned, favorite moments; discuss continuing the innovation project
Award printed Student Participation Certificates to each member
Talk about next steps: another FLL season, or connecting with an FTC/FRC team for progression
deliverables: Season reflections captured in the notebook

meetings.title: Wrap-up part 2: disassembly + inventory
goals: Return all materials to season-ready state
activities: Disassemble the robot and all mission models (TMG post-season list)
Inventory the SPIKE Prime set and BIOGLOW Challenge Set; note missing pieces (LEGO replacement-parts page if needed)
Archive programs, the Engineering Notebook, photos, and scoresheets for next season's team
Final reflection circle and thank-yous; store mat, table, and materials

slides.title: Core Values
slides.tip: Introduce the FIRST Core Values — collaboration, respect, teamwork, learning, inclusion — expressed as Gracious Professionalism and Coopertition.

slides.title: Overview – Core Values
points: Demonstrate FIRST Core Values in everything you do — your team will be evaluated during the robot game and the judging session.
Apply teamwork and discovery to explore the challenge.
Innovate with new ideas about your robot and project.
Show how your team and your solutions will have an impact and be inclusive!
Celebrate by having fun in everything you do!

slides.title: Overview – Innovation Project
points: Prepare a live, engaging presentation to explain the work you have done on your innovation project.
Identify and research a problem.
Design a new solution or improve an existing one based on your selected idea, brainstorming, and plan.
Create a model, drawing, or prototype.
Iterate on your solution by sharing it with others and collecting feedback.
Communicate your solution's potential impact.

slides.title: Overview – Robot Design
points: Prepare a short explanation of your robot design, programs, and strategy.
Identify your mission strategy.
Design your robot and programs and create an effective plan.
Create your robot and programming solution.
Iterate, test, and improve your robot and program.
Communicate your robot design process and everyone's contributions.

slides.title: Overview – Robot Game
points: Your team will have three 2.5-minute matches to complete as many missions as possible.
Build the mission models and set up the field mat.
Review the missions and rules.
Design and build a robot.
Explore building and coding skills while practicing with your robot on the mat.
Compete at an event!

Design Your Robot
Use the Engineering Design Process and Core Values

slides.title: Team Journey

Create Your Robot Solution
Iterate Your Solutions and Receive Feedback to Improve

slides.title: Team Roles
points: Researcher — investigates ideas and finds relevant research from different sources to inform the team's decision-making.
Creative Designer — creates innovative designs for solutions to be discussed with the team.
Team Captain — shares team progress with facilitator; ensures session tasks are completed.
Project Manager — focuses on time management and preparing for the event.
Communicator — concentrates on how to communicate the team's work; writes scripts and prepares presentations.

slides.title: Team Roles
points: Builder — assembles the LEGO mission models following the building instructions and builds your robot.
Material Manager — gathers and returns materials needed for the session.
Coder — operates the device and creates the programs in the app.
Mission Strategist — analyzes the Robot Game Rulebook and leads team strategy discussions on which missions to attempt.

slides.title: Materials Needed
points: LEGO Education SPIKE Prime Set
Electronic Device
Note: Other LEGO Education sets such as MINDSTORMS and Robot Inventor are also allowed.

slides.title: Materials Needed – BIOGLOW Challenge Set
points: The Challenge Set box contains the mission models, challenge mat, 3M Dual Lock fasteners, coach pins, and season tiles for team members.
The team should build the models very carefully using the building instructions.

slides.title: Materials Needed – Challenge Mat and Table
points: Set up a table with the challenge mat in your classroom or meeting space.
Teams can practice on the mat by placing it on the floor.
Robot game matches at official events will be played on a table complete with sidewalls.
Instructions to build a table can be found on the Season Resources page.

slides.title: Project Sparks

slides.title: Project Sparks

slides.title: Project Sparks

slides.title: Introduction
points: Get to know your team.
Record information about your team here.
Select a team name.
slides.tip: Have the team watch the season videos on the FIRST LEGO League YouTube channel and read pages 3-9 in their Engineering Notebooks.

slides.title: Key Vocabulary
points: mission model: The LEGO models placed on the field, designed to represent a real-world concept or challenge.
project spark: provides guidance on selection of the project problem.
innovation project: identify a problem and develop a solution to solve it.

paperwork.item: Team registration with the local Program Delivery Partner (Pre-Season Checkpoint)

paperwork.item: Signed consent/participation forms (sent home at the Aug 11 kickoff)

paperwork.item: Printed Field Setup Guide (4-up color) as table-reset checklist

paperwork.item: Innovation Project Planning sheet (Engineering Notebook p29) — all boxes

paperwork.item: Robot Design Notes / mission notes (Engineering Notebook p30, photocopied per mission) + model notes (p10)
